PullRequest.Title: sessions: move artifact details general actions into the header
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## What

The artifact details panel (opened from an artifact pill in the chat input) showed its general actions, such as Open Pull Request Changes, Copy Link and Remove Artifact, in a separate footer row below Autopilot. They now render as icon-only buttons in the header toolbar, to the left of Close, and the footer row is removed.

- Each icon's hover and accessible name give the full action label, including any reason the action is unavailable or running (for example "Merge. Checks must pass.").
- Remove Artifact uses the trash glyph in the header so it is not confused with the adjacent Close button. Other surfaces keep their existing icon.
- Header buttons are compact 22px squares that stay on one row. When the title would be squeezed in a narrow pane, the actions move to a row below the title instead of breaking it mid-word.
- Keyboard order is: title, the general actions, Close, then the panel body. The accessibility help text, design notes, and a comment are updated to describe the header placement.

## Why

The footer consumed a full row of vertical space in a panel that is already height-constrained above the chat input.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, open a session that has a recorded pull request artifact and select its pill.
2. The header shows the general actions as icons before Close; there is no footer row.
3. Hover each icon: the hover names the action. Tab from the title through the icons to Close; Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the pill.
4. Select Open Pull Request Changes so the editor opens and the chat pane narrows, then reopen the details: the title wraps by word and the icons move below it.

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/chat/artifactIntegrationPresentation.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/chat/artifactIntegrationGroup.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/chat/sessionArtifacts.test.ts`: 167 passing. Includes a new layout test that fails with the previous header rules.
- `pnpm run eslint` on the changed TypeScript files: passed.
- Component Explorer: the `sessions/artifactIntegrations` and `sessions/artifactDetails` fixtures render without errors. Screenshot baselines for the details-panel fixtures are expected to change.
- Manually verified in a Code OSS Agents window with a real pull request artifact: hover labels, keyboard order, running an action from the header, and the narrow-pane layout.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an artifact pill and render the artifact-details panel, including a recorded pull request with main/checks/comments details.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The context view synchronously creates the details model and panel and can render loading state immediately. Each unique details lease then completes before that section has authoritative content; those asynchronous acquisitions are not newly placed on initial panel construction by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire and subscribe to provider details; remote extension/agent-host implementations cross their protocol boundary and may trigger provider network refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One acquisition per effective unique (integrationId, detailsId), deduplicated by the wanted Map. The concrete pull-request view exposes up to main, checks, and comments, so a typical fully populated PR is three acquisitions rather than one per section/item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening the same panel created the same leases and made the same protocol/provider calls; only the already-produced general-action buttons were rendered in a footer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The panel opens with loading state, but each section's useful details depend on its acquisition response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Maintain or raise the artifact provider's interactive details subscription, which can refresh GitHub pull-request core, checks, and review-thread data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The three PR details models share the underlying resource; each lease updates the same subscription interests rather than issuing a new request per displayed row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical details leases and subscription priority changes occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fresh remote data is needed for authoritative details, while cached snapshot state can render first.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of unique details IDs across contributions after Map deduplication, typically 1-3 for the PR integration; item count affects existing list rendering but not the moved header actions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ArtifactDetailsModel starts one asynchronous acquire per deduplicated integration/details key without a shared limiter. ArtifactBinding coalesces concurrent references to the same detailsId and reference-counts disposal. This behavior and concurrency are unchanged by the header move.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ArtifactBinding caches a provider details model by detailsId while references exist and coalesces concurrent same-key leases; the final release removes and disposes it. Provider snapshots can supply warm state, while a cold/opened subscription may refresh remotely. The diff changes neither keys, positive/negative states, coalescing, nor release lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor, lease deduplication, protocol path, provider subscription, and reference-counted cache were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider implementations vary in remote refresh cost, but the diff does not add, duplicate, or move these calls onto a new critical path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The expensive acquisition path and its cardinality are unchanged; the diff only relocates a small keyed action set.

Scenarios.Scenario: Live artifact updates and user invocation of a general action such as Open Pull Request Changes, Copy Link, Remove Artifact, Sign In, or provider Refresh.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A snapshot/details observable update synchronously projects view data and updates the existing keyed button widgets, then requests layout. A user action performs exactly one existing action callback; completion depends on that action's existing IPC/network/editor boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke a provider action or request authentication when the selected general action is provider-owned.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One invocation per user click, independent of the number of header buttons.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same footer button called the same callback once per click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The selected action waits for its existing provider/authentication operation; merely rendering it in the header performs no invocation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/browser/chat/artifactDetailsModel.ts:generalActions shell action mapping; src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/browser/chat/sessionArtifacts.ts recorded artifact toolbar actions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open pull-request changes/editor content, copy a link, remove the recorded artifact, or open a resource through the existing shell toolbar action callback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shell callback per click; realistic header cardinality is a small set (for a recorded PR, open changes/copy/remove plus any provider action).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The footer exposed and ran the identical action object; the diff changes icon/placement only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Action-specific work is on the clicked command's critical path, not panel refresh or hover.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of general actions, ordinarily a few; each live update performs O(actions) keyed updates as before, with one additional constant close-button update.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Button updates are synchronous and keyed by action id. Layout is coalesced to at most one scheduled animation-frame request. User clicks are not newly parallelized or fanned out by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ArtifactButtons retains and reuses widgets by stable action id, disposing only removed ids. The moved actions use this same cache/lifecycle pattern as the former footer. No result cache or negative-cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the before/after renderer path, keyed DisposableMap behavior, and click callbacks were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Update frequency depends on provider polling/activity, but action cardinality is bounded in realistic integrations and the only added work is one constant keyed close-button reset.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. General actions already underwent O(actions) DOM updates; combining Close adds only constant work and introduces no boundary fan-out or retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize or narrow the Agents/chat pane while artifact details are open, causing the title and header actions to share one row or wrap to two rows.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CSS flex layout wraps the whole action group below the title when necessary. ResizeObserver schedules the existing panel layout at the next animation frame; panel.layout performs existing geometry reads and scrollbar scans.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Pane resize frequency and a small number of header actions; flex layout grows with header children, not artifact list-item count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Resize-driven layout requests are coalesced by pendingLayout to one animation-frame callback. Browser style/layout work is synchronous in that callback, with no worker, subprocess, or queue fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No data cache is involved. The pending-layout disposable is the coalescing state and is cleared on hide/disposal; this lifecycle is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the CSS, ResizeObserver sources, animation-frame guard, and synchronous layout reads were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact browser layout cost varies by platform and width, but the changed flex rules affect only one small header and do not establish frame-scale repeated work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Wrapping can add one header line, but resize work remains frame-coalesced and bounded to a small toolbar.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all nine changed files and traced opening, live updates/action execution, resize/layout, provider acquisition, caching, concurrency, and disposal. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
